description: Re-levels the soundtrack of a clip that is already rendered, without re-rendering it - the fix for a finished video flagged as clipping (an 'audio_clipped' warning or a 'full_scale' finding), on the CPU in seconds. 'clip' is the video: an 'output:' ref to a finished run's file or an 'asset:' ref. A first step normalizes the clip's own soundtrack so its loudest sample sits at 'peak_dbfs' (-3 leaves the headroom an AAC encode needs); give 'target_lufs' to gain it to that integrated loudness first, with 'peak_dbfs' still the ceiling. A second step muxes the leveled track back onto the same clip. The video stream is re-encoded, not copied: one generation of encode loss, the cost of not re-rendering. A clip with no audio fails at the first step.
summary: Fix a clipping soundtrack on an already-rendered clip: normalize its audio and mux it back, CPU only.
